decision: D-009 v4 vs v3 test, photoreal half (hi l01, l08, l10)

method.check_1_words: Local whisper.cpp ggml-small transcript (lang hi, no prompt) compared with the script words, including the English words inside the Hindi. Pass = every script word is recognisable, nothing is added or missing. whisper-small Hindi spelling noise (दाउत for doubt, ताना for था ना) is not counted as a miss. ElevenLabs Scribe did run on two takes, but its text cannot be read back in this session (see not_checked).
method.check_2_tags: Pass = no tag word (laughs, giddy, excited, fast, calm, quietly, slowly, deliberate, sighs, weary) in the transcript. Non-speech (laugh, sigh) is located with a 20/40 ms RMS envelope and a 70-300 Hz voiced-frame proxy.
method.check_3_length: Speech span (clip minus leading and trailing silence at -40 dB, ffmpeg silencedetect) within +/-20% of target_seconds.
method.check_4_quiet_tag: Only where the line carries a whispered or quiet tag (l08 [quietly]). Level of the tagged second half against the same take's untagged first half (active-frame RMS, frames above -45 dBFS). Pass = at least 3 dB lower, still voiced, and the words still transcribed. The 3 dB bar was set after the levels had been measured, so the sensitivity at a 1 dB bar is reported too. l01 and l10 carry no quiet tag, so check 4 is n/a there.
method.pair_rule: Each check is scored pass or fail per take. A pair goes to the model that passes more checks; equal counts are a tie. D-009: a tie stays with v4.

pairs.speaker: tara

v4.transcript: चालिस लाग फिम्रान और उसे दाउत तक नहीं हूँ
v4.notes: Laugh present: ~0.9 s of breathy unvoiced pulses before 'चालीस' (voiced share 0.12). The laugh is most of the overrun.

v3.transcript: चालिस लाक हिम्रान और से दाउट तत नहीं हूँ.
v3.notes: [laughs] looks ignored: speech starts at 0.18 s at full level straight into 'चालीस', with no non-speech segment. 10 dB hotter than v4 (mean -12.8 dB, peak -0.4 dBFS). Trailing silence 0.00 s, so the tail may be clipped.

pairs.caveat: v3 wins on length only, and partly because it drops the directed laugh, which the four checks do not score. On the brief's intent (is the laugh real) the measurements favour v4.

pairs.speaker: imran

v4.notes: Sigh is a 0.56 s unvoiced breath (voiced share 0.07), then ~0.3 s of near-silence. Overrun +0.58 s.

v3.notes: Sigh is a 0.53 s unvoiced breath (voiced share 0.00), straight into the words. 'बोला था ना' is 4.4 dB louder than v4 (-20.4 vs -24.8 dB); whether that tips it towards menace needs the ear.

pairs.caveat: v4 misses the length bar by 3 points with one take per model, so a second v4 take could easily land inside it.

result.d009_status: Not settled by this scene. v3 needs at least 4 of the 6 pairs; with 2 here it needs at least 2 of the 3 flat-2D pairs (l07, l08, l12). If l08 is read at a 1 dB bar, v3 has 3 here and needs 1 of 3.
result.per_character_note: No case for moving a single character to v3. Both v4 voices did their non-verbal tags (Tara's laugh, Imran's sigh). v3 ignored Tara's laugh. Neither model obeyed [quietly] on the caller.
result.strength_of_evidence: Weak. One take per model per line. Both v3 wins come from the length check alone, one of them by 3 points and one by dropping a directed laugh. Length on single takes is noisy.
result.owner_override: Per D-009 the owner's pick by ear overrides this.
